name: Does a bump-out addition require a concrete foundation?

mainEntity.name: Does a bump-out addition require a concrete foundation?

acceptedAnswer.text: Whether your bump-out requires a foundation depends on the distance the structure extends from your exterior wall. Small bump-outs extending about two to three feet can often be cantilevered, meaning existing floor joists are extended outward without touching the ground beneath. For bump-outs extending deeper, such as four to ten feet, building codes typically require structural ground support such as concrete footings, piers, or a continuous stem wall foundation. The decision factor comes down to structural load and soil support; cantilevering avoids digging but limits total depth and heavy floor loads, whereas footings support heavy features like large tile showers or masonry.
acceptedAnswer.description: Small bump-outs up to three feet can often cantilever from existing floor joists, while deeper extensions require ground support like concrete footings or stem walls.
